en: In the *Buddhabhāṣita-āyuṣpramāṇa-sūtra*,
at that time the World-Honored One was between the twin śāla trees, on the verge of parinirvāṇa.
There were the fourfold assembly— bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās— who all gathered together.
[Name] extended his life. Kneeling with palms joined,
he came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Blessed One, we fourfold assemblies have all gathered here to entreat the Tathāgata:
do not enter parinirvāṇa."
We only pray that the Tathāgata will compassionately accept our exhortation and remain for one kalpa;
do not enter parinirvāṇa.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Yan-shou:
"Listen attentively, for I shall now analyze this for you. From the time [the teaching was first established] until the present, forty-nine years have passed."
He teaches and transforms sentient beings,
from the birds above down to the ants below.
All wriggling and moving sentient beings—whether with form or without form;
four-footed, two-footed, many-footed, or footless;
born from a womb, an egg, moisture, or transformation.
In this way, I shall cause all sentient beings to encounter spiritual friends and attain perfect enlightenment. [Bestow upon me...
I now wish to enter nirvana.
This was originally requested by Pāpīyān. Pāpīyān said to me:
"Gautama, all sentient beings within the triple world undergo birth and death."
"Gautama, if you were to remain for even a single kalpa today,
it would contradict my original vow.
At that time, I accepted the invitation of Pāpīyān.
And enter into nirvana.
I am opposed by Pāpīyān;
how could I be like the Buddhas?
Bodhisattva Yanshou addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, Pāpīyas has manifested his life-span outside [the realm], and while the various Buddhas enter nirvana,
he intends to become the sovereign of the triple world."
All sentient beings have entirely entered the net of Māra; there is no rest,
as they pass from birth and death to birth and death.
From affliction to affliction,
they constantly serve as the retinue of Māra and do not encounter the True Dharma.
Furthermore, upon death they enter hell,
where for thousands and tens of thousands of kalpas there is constant darkness.
There are blades as large as wheels, copper snakes, and iron dogs.
The ox-headed hell-wardens have hands like sharp blades, as piercing as frost and snow;
from morning until night they seize and drag one another,
causing boundless terror.
There is no place to hide;
they do not even hear the names of their parents or the Triple Gem.
Within a single day, they undergo thousands of births and ten thousands of deaths.
Emerging from hell, they again undergo various evil births,
receiving bodies such as those of camels or being born among donkeys.
They constantly carry heavy burdens and are perpetually afflicted by hunger and thirst;
if born among humans, they will be poor and lowly,
driven into service by others.
Their clothing does not cover their bodies;
their food does not fill their mouths.
Or there are those who are wealthy and noble yet have no sons or daughters.
Some may be impoverished yet have many children;
some sentient beings may suffer from malignant sores upon their beds, becoming emaciated and gravely ill,
their forms wasting away and their flesh consumed over the course of years and months.
Malignant sores and pus and blood flow constantly from their entire bodies;
they are loathed and despised by others,
or suffer from blindness, deafness, or muteness.
Some do not die for a hundred years yet suffer;
others are wealthy and noble for thirty years before dying young.
Thus they are unjustly struck by calamity.
They have all entered the net of Māra.
We pray only that the Tathāgata will remain for one kalpa and not accept the invitation of Pāpīyān.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Yanshou: "Good son,
after my parinirvāṇa, if there are sentient beings..."
They undergo such various evil retributions; yet,
by merely creating one hundred fascicles of the *Yanshou jing*, or even as few as one or two fascicles—
just as the strength of a single person is not equal to the strength of ten people— [the merit is immeasurable].
The strength of ten people is not equal to that of a hundred;
it is the same when it comes to producing this *Yanshou jing*.
One should simply produce this sūtra, distribute it to others, and cause them to receive, uphold, read, and recite it.
I shall rescue and protect them.
It is like a compassionate mother who has given birth to an only son;
if the son falls ill, the compassionate mother also falls ill.
If you are healed, your compassionate mother will also be healed. Good son,
all sentient beings are my children.
"To those who make virtuous vows, I shall extend my golden hand;
as if stroking their crowns with it, there shall be no fulfillment of their original vows that is not attained.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Extending Life praised him in verse:
The World-Honored One, possessing the marks of a great man and the hue of true gold, is fully adorned with the eighty secondary characteristics.
For forty-nine years, the Great Compassionate Father has remained; yet Pāpīyān, for no reason, requested his entry into *nirvāṇa*.
Now that he is as tranquil and invisible as space, one knows with certainty that there shall never again be birth within the three realms.
The Buddha-dharma will perish, and calamities will arise; the Māras, with their poisonous hearts, will compete against one another.

All the śrāvakas and bodhisattvas, all the people and the fourfold assembly—the river of Dharma will run dry, the banner of Dharma will be toppled, the mountain of Dharma will collapse, and the ship of Dharma will sink.
The kings of the eight nations all beat their breasts; Blood and sweat flow like tears in a torrential rain.
Who would have expected that the Great Master would enter Nirvana? We commoners shall remain for even longer.
The Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas cry out, "Excellent! All sentient beings have lost their refuge.
At that time, there was a great bodhisattva in the assembly named Pujing (Universal Purity),
who questioned the Bodhisattva Yanshou (Prolonging Life).
The Tathāgata enters nirvāṇa today;
with what shall he entrust the sentient beings in the evil realms so that they may attain long life?
"Do not be like the Tathāgata, who is the foremost in the three realms,
yet does not remain for even one kalpa.
At that time, Yanshou addressed him, saying:
The Bodhisattva Pujing,
after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, caused one hundred fascicles of the *Yanshou jing* (Sūtra on Extending Life) to be transcribed and distributed among sentient beings.
They recited it together,
whereby short-lived sentient beings were granted long life.
Through the Tathāgata’s great compassion, he extended his golden arm to stroke their heads and bestow upon them the prediction of enlightenment.
"The Tathāgata shall protect himself.
At that time, Pujin praised him, saying,
"Excellent, excellent!"
Having received these words,
which are certainly not false,
we accept them with faith and shall practice accordingly.
The Scripture on Prolonging Life Spoken by the Buddha, one fascicle.
